originalTitle: DraftKings Gains Legal Ground on Prediction Markets, but Its Quarterly EBITDA Loss Reaches $317 Million

content:
We just published our list of the 10 Best High-Growth Stocks to Diversify Away From Big Tech , and Draftkings Inc. ranked 7th on the list.

The S&P 500 has grown notably top-heavy. The 10 largest companies currently make up about 40% of its value, compared to 20% to 25% for the most of the period since 1980, while technology accounts for nearly 40% of the standard index but only roughly 16% of the equal-weight version. That focus paid off while AI spending boosted the biggest names. That said, things have started to become costly.

On November 19, the S&P 500 dropped 2.02% to 7,175.83, the Nasdaq Composite sank 2.25% to 23,879.20, and the Dow closed below 50,000. Anthropic's IPO failed to revive the AI trade, and the S&P 500 fell further below its 200-day moving average. Readers interested in the stocks hardest impacted by the latest sequence of tech selloffs can see more in our list of oversold AI stocks that continue to draw analyst interest , and those who want to stay in the buildout can read more about these AI infrastructure stocks to buy for the long-term .

Calls to spread risk have getting been louder across the market. Dryden Pence, chief investment officer at Pence Capital, favors an equal-weight S&P 500 as a core holding because ten stocks make up roughly 40% of the S&P 500 and 50% of the Nasdaq. Moreover, according to Credo's Benjamin Newton, equal weight increases exposure to industrials, financials, and healthcare. Earnings support the case. Russell Investments said analysts expected third-quarter earnings growth of 20.3% for the Magnificent Seven and 27.7% for the rest of the 493 S&P 500 companies.

The case for looking beyond mega-cap technology is that major tech companies have kept expanding. Their valuations already account for a significant amount of the projected AI-driven earnings acceleration, while an array of healthcare, industrial, consumer, finance, and energy companies are expanding at rates that might surprise investors.

With that in mind, let's take a look at the 10 best high-growth stocks to diversify away from Big Tech. The stocks below are distinct from our previous coverage of high-growth stocks outside Big Tech , which screened for non-tech companies with a 5-year EPS growth of at least 25%. Readers who want more ideas beyond the mega-caps can make use of both lists.

DraftKings qualifies with a three-year revenue growth rate of 39.3%. Its demand is driven by sports betting and prediction markets instead of Big Tech spending, and 51 hedge funds owned the stock as of the third quarter.

The gambling giant reported third-quarter revenue of $1.329 billion, up 16% year-over-year from $1.144 billion. The rise was led by increased customer engagement and a stronger Sportsbook net revenue margin, with monthly unique payers up 13% and sports consumer volume up 22%. The profitability picture was less bright. The company recorded a net loss of $468.7 million, higher than the $256.8 million loss a year before, while adjusted EBITDA was negative $316.9 million, compared to a loss of $126.5 million in the prior-year quarter. The decrease was mostly caused by increased investment in Predictions, DraftKings' prediction-markets division.

That said, the legal situation has improved. Earlier this year, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals concluded that sports-related prediction-market contracts were not "swaps" under federal commodities law, allowing Nevada to apply its gaming restrictions and refusing Kalshi, Crypto.com, and Robinhood's injunction requests. DraftKings stock jumped as much to 10% following the news. For DraftKings, the challenge is to translate a more favorable regulatory environment into earnings growth. Our coverage examines whether the prediction-market ruling provides DraftKings a long-term competitive advantage .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of DKNG as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. If you're looking for an extremely undervalued AI stock that also stands to benefit significantly from Trump-era tariffs and the onshoring trend, see our free report on the best short-term AI stock .
